_README: The words ShootScript refuses to let onto Cari's shooting copy. Anything inside [[notes]] is exempt — that is the whole point of notes. Add a word by adding an object to `banned` (ERROR) or `house_jargon` (WARN). `pattern` is a Python regex; `case_sensitive` defaults to false.

banned.why: "in and out" is an editor's join. Cari shoots what is happening.
IN 1 / OUT 2 are weld labels from the edit, not directions.
entry/exit lines are an editor's idea. On her copy it is just a line.
a weld is a cut between two pieces of tape — nothing to shoot.
a bridge is an edit structure. Say what happens in front of the camera.
attach points describe where a piece lands in the cut.
THEREFORE/BUT joints are story-structure notes for the edit.
a shouted THEREFORE/BUT is a joint marker from the edit.
"serving" is house shorthand for a chunk of the film in the edit.
the spine is the edit's running order, not a shooting instruction.
beat ids (P1, beat 4) mean nothing on the day.
a clip id is a reference to a file. Write a plain synopsis instead.
a camera clip id. Write a plain synopsis instead.
a camera roll/clip id. Write a plain synopsis instead.
timecode belongs in the edit, not on a shooting copy.

house_jargon.why: not sourced anywhere Cari can read — define with Jason.
PTC is real industry shorthand, but spell it out the first time.
on a homestead shoot "the vehicle" reads as the truck.
house word for how the strands interlock — needs Jason's definition.
"pickup" is industry; the A/B labels are edit bookkeeping.

house_jargon.industry: title card / question card / memory card
house_jargon.why: means three different things to the two of you.
a call sheet and a shot list already exist as words.
genuinely a house form; keep it, but define it in the glossary.

_voice_note: Cari, Sep 19 2026: a line she hands Jason is a line he SAYS, so it is written in the first person ("I can't afford the crusher"), and a question she asks is written the way she would ask it, to him ("You told me X — where were you coming from?"). Action stays third person present, as screenplays do.
_forward_note: These match a reference to somewhere ELSE IN THE PAPER, never a thing happening in front of the camera. 'the hammer coming up into his hand' and 'the earth below' are action; 'see below' and 'coming up later' are not.
